findings.text: Upheld as advisory (question 2): the forget step (dropRepoRows plus the knowledge_repos delete in one withWrite) is written in both rebuildAll and refreshOne (line 807). One forgetRepo(db, id) helper would hold it. Only one statement is repeated.
Upheld as advisory (question 2): refreshOne repeats ensureFresh's freshness predicate (head and fingerprint, line 781). One shared predicate would do.
Upheld as advisory (question 2): searchEntries builds its placeholders inline although the placeholders helper defined just above does the same.
Upheld as advisory (question 2): TypeSafeJudge.relate and heuristic relate (heuristic.ts:248) repeat the same RelateInput-to-ConsolidateTexts mapping and the same id-to-index verdict mapping.
Upheld as advisory (questions 2 and 6): the kind list is restated in four places (entry.ts:9, tools.ts:71, render.ts:100, opencode-plugin.ts:92) and nothing ties them together.
Upheld as advisory (question 2): KNOWLEDGE_LINE copies contribute.ts's intro and count wording as regex literals. Only a test ties the copies; the architecture gate's F-2 names the same issue.
Upheld as advisory (question 9): getKnowledge calls freshen before its own REF check. The zod schema rejects such a ref first on every tool path, so the inner check is either dead or too late.
Upheld as advisory (question 9): the ?? "workspace" fallback cannot be reached, and if it ever were, it would mislabel a proposal without any warning.
Upheld as advisory (questions 4 and 5): proposeKnowledge's KnowledgeError catch duplicates runTool's catch at line 491 on its only production path.
Upheld as advisory (questions 2 and 6): the catch writes checkedAgentId's message again by hand instead of printing error.message.
Upheld as advisory (question 5): pinnedLine only forwards to entryLine.

Upheld as advisory (question 6): three catches (lines 713, 743, 752) find a missing table by matching the error message, while status and compact ask sqlite_master. The change has two ways of answering one question.
Upheld as advisory (question 1): knowledgeRepositories is about 250 lines and does several separate jobs. It is still one check.
Upheld as advisory (question 9): an unreadable rate row silently resets the window with nothing logged. Only this code writes that row.

Upheld as advisory (question 1, one clause): no test would fail if the knowledge_shown prune ran in its own transaction after the session delete, so AC-27's 'same transaction' clause is held only by a code comment. The rest of the criterion is covered.

Upheld as advisory (question 1, structural clause): no test tells one transaction per repository apart from one transaction with a catch per repository. The visible outcome (the other repositories are still rebuilt) is proven.

Upheld as advisory (question 5): the 'by rowid' check runs EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN on the exported constants (also at line 337). It is coupled to the implementation and would not fail if the writer stopped using those constants.

Upheld as advisory (auth): a client can rotate its handshake name to get about 12 rate windows. Part 1's quotas still cap the volume, every proposal still needs a person's acceptance, and ADR 0024 records that the id is not authenticated.

Upheld as advisory (public-api, hardening): knowledge_search.query has no maximum length, and knowledge_propose.body is bounded only after redaction. A local agent can pass an unbounded string; nothing is exposed.

Upheld as advisory (personal-data): knowledge_get puts the entry's author name in the agent's context, and ADR 0024's personal-data section names only on_behalf_of. Today the author is always the local person, so nobody new sees the name.

Advisory, outside this item: the hard-coded plural reads '1 projects' (review/ui/settings-sharing-problems@1512.png). The line belongs to sibling item 2026-11-09-002, which was ruled in its own round.
Advisory, outside this item: the problems alert reads as a log line (review/ui/settings-sharing-problems@1512.png). It is sibling item 2026-11-09-002's line; the reviewer files it as advisory copy.
Advisory, outside this item: the sharing pill is drawn under the Links column (review/ui/projects-row-pill-knowledge@1512.png). It is sibling item 2026-11-09-002's line.

Lowered to advisory. Question 10 would make a console error a defect, but two things hold it back. First, the line is sibling item 2026-11-09-002's interface, ruled under its own item, not this item's change. Second, the error is the browser's network log of the 500 that the error state provokes on purpose (review/ui/console-settings-sharing-error.json), and the page handles it with a plain toast. The reviewer also gives the line only approximately.

Advisory, outside this item: the disabled radio list looks almost the same as the enabled one (review/ui/projects-dock-no-remote@1512.png). It is sibling item 2026-11-09-002's line, and the reviewer gives the line only approximately.
Advisory, debt: the compact preview does not show the new knowledgeShown count. AC-25 asks only that the route carry the count, and ui/src/api.ts:137 does.

Upheld as advisory (question 1): in a session that reuses an id and has no session start, INSERT OR IGNORE keeps the stale row, so an entry can be shown again on matching prompts. It needs the rare reused-id state and is bounded at 2 entries in 480 characters. No defect condition of the rubric is met.

Upheld as advisory (question 6): the release-day order (version bump, bun run plugins, binary before the OpenCode package) is named without an owner or order. The rubric lists 'a manual step the plan names without an owner' as an advisory. It is not a dependency the spec leaves unstated.
Upheld as advisory (question 5): 'parts 1 to 3 ship in one release' is a dependency the spec states. Nothing enforces it, but a stated dependency is not a defect.
Upheld as advisory (questions 1 and 4): no status line shows the tools' TypeSafe counters or the open proposals. The cost and the volume are capped in code, and the ADR states the gap.
Upheld as advisory (question 4): the tools share distillation's persisted breaker. This is stated, logged, visible in doctor, and recovers on its own.
Upheld as advisory (question 1): when the timeout fires after the write has committed, the agent gets an empty answer. A retry is caught as a duplicate, so nothing is written twice.
Upheld as advisory (question 1): a project folder emptied by hand keeps its indexed rows until a write or a rebuild. The limit is stated; no doctor signal is named for it.

Upheld as advisory: rootAreas is a second hand reader of the taxonomy file, copying taxonomyFor. CLAUDE.md names doctor as the only one, so a guard added to taxonomyFor later would not reach rootAreas. It runs no git.
Upheld as advisory: KNOWLEDGE_LINE is not built from contribute.ts's exported constants, so a wording change would silently stop the stripping. This repeats code-quality's F-6.
Upheld as advisory: ADR 0019's contract paragraph does not mention the ToolCall and globalInstructions additions. ADR 0024 records them.
Upheld as advisory: ConsolidateTexts types the text as plain string where it leaves the machine. Both entry points still require Redacted, so nothing leaks today.
Upheld as advisory: the forget-a-gone-repository step is written twice (here and at 757-761). Both copies sit behind the same refusals. This repeats code-quality's F-1.
Advisory, debt: taxonomyFor belongs to part 1 (item 2026-11-08-003) and does not call refuseLinkedRoots.
Upheld as advisory (questions 2 and 6): the FTS search runs under BEGIN IMMEDIATE, and its repo_id filter on an UNINDEXED column scales with the whole corpus. It is measured within the prompt budget.
Upheld as advisory (question 2): pinnedEntries scans every entry row of the visible repositories to find the pins; a partial index would read only the pins. It is measured within budget.
Upheld as advisory (question 6): nothing deletes the knowledge.rate:<agent id> meta rows, so their number has no fixed bound. Each row is small and holds no personal data.
Advisory, debt: sessions.id can be reused because it has no AUTOINCREMENT. The guards this item adds hold.
